messages.subject: Your account will be suspended in 24 hours
messages.body:
Dear customer,

We detected unusual sign-in activity on your account. To avoid permanent suspension, verify your identity within 24 hours.
clues: Urgent threat to push you into acting without thinking
Sender domain is a lookalike, not the bank's real one
The link goes to verify-login.co, a different domain entirely
Generic greeting: “Dear customer”

messages.subject: Planned maintenance this Saturday 22:00–23:00
messages.body:
Hi Priya,

Email and VPN will be unavailable on Saturday between 22:00 and 23:00 while we install updates. No action is needed from you. Questions? Reply here or call extension 4410.
clues: Comes from your organisation's real domain
Asks you to do nothing: no link, no login, no attachment
Specific, checkable details and a known way to contact IT

messages.subject: ParcelGo delivery
messages.body: ParcelGo: your parcel is held at our depot due to an unpaid customs fee of £1.99. Pay within 12 hours or it will be returned.
clues: A tiny fee is bait to collect your full card details
Unexpected parcel from an unknown mobile number
Odd domain (.help) that isn't the courier's site
Deadline pressure

messages.subject: Quick favour
messages.body: Are you at your desk? I need you to buy five £100 gift cards for a client right away. I'm in meetings all day so just email me the codes. Please keep this between us for now.
clues: The “CEO” is using a personal Gmail address
Gift cards are a classic scam payment because they can't be traced
Asks for secrecy and bypasses normal process
Uses authority and urgency together

messages.subject: Reset your Fabrikam password
messages.body: You asked to reset the password for your Fabrikam account a minute ago. This link expires in 30 minutes. If you didn't ask for this, you can ignore this email and your password won't change.
clues: You just requested it, so it's expected
The link stays on the company's own domain
No threats; it tells you it's safe to ignore
Still, when in doubt, type the site address yourself

messages.subject: Invoice_0932.pdf has been shared with you
messages.body:
A document has been shared with you. Sign in with your work email and password to view it.

Attachment: Invoice_0932.pdf.html
clues: Double extension: “.pdf.html” is a web page pretending to be a PDF
Asks for your work password just to view a file
An invoice you weren't expecting
Sender domain doesn't match any service you use

messages.subject: Your books are due back on 14 March
messages.body:
Hello Sam,

The two books on your card are due back on 14 March. You can renew them by signing in at woodgrovelibrary.org or at any branch.
clues: Expected message from a service you use
Points you to the real site instead of a sign-in link
Personal greeting and no pressure

messages.subject: Mailbox 98% full: action required
messages.body: Your mailbox has almost reached its limit. You will stop receiving new email today unless you increase your storage.
clues: Pretends to be internal IT but comes from an outside lookalike domain
Threatens a consequence (no more email) to rush you
The link leads to a fake sign-in page
